J1_line_asserts_challenged_proposition.justification: The response challenges 'The proof claims that any walk between two vertices in a tree must be a path because the tree is circuit-free.' First-choice line 7 is 'By def., tree is circuit-free, so P_1 is a path (since path has no repeated edges and no repeated vertices)'. The active assumptions at that point are line 5 (u, v distinct vertices of a tree T) and line 6 ('there is a walk P_1 between u and v'), which fixes no property of P_1 beyond being a u-v walk; line 7 then infers pathhood from circuit-freeness alone. So the line does assert the inference the response attacks, for an arbitrary walk supplied by line 6.

J2_evidence_specified.justification: 'In the tree consisting of the edges u-x and x-v, the walk u-x-u-x-v connects u to v but repeats vertex x and the edge u-x, yet contains no circuit (no closed trail).' The graph, its edge set, the two endpoints and the explicit walk are all given.

J3_evidence_check.justification: Checked the supplied witness by finite enumeration (scripts/P08_check.py). The graph on {u,x,v} with edges ux, xv is connected with |E| = |V|-1 and has no cycle of length >= 3 (brute-force over all vertex sequences), so it is a tree and is circuit-free, satisfying the source's hypotheses at lines 5-7, and u != v. The sequence u-x-u-x-v has every consecutive pair an edge, so it is a walk between u and v admissible as the P_1 of line 6; it repeats the vertex x (and u) and the edge ux, so it is not a path under the very definition line 7 cites ('no repeated edges and no repeated vertices'). Hence with all of the source's assumptions in force the conclusion of line 7 fails, which refutes the inference as written. One interpretive step is mine and not computational: reading line 6's 'there is a walk P_1' as leaving P_1 unconstrained, so that this walk is an admissible P_1.

J4_consequence_overreach.justification: The final answer states only that the located claim is false ('showing the claim is false'); it asserts no consequence for the theorem being proved (uniqueness of paths in a tree), and the visible reasoning in fact observes that the gap is repairable ('you need to argue that any walk can be reduced to a path').
